context: When Proteor acquired Filament Innovations, my role as CTO carried forward as Lead R&D Engineer.

bullets.text: Led the design and development of the ICARUS-Lite, a compact industrial printer that automates prosthetic and orthotic production with minimal customer setup. Owned its mechanical, electrical, and software design, including custom AC heaters.
Owned the ICARUS-Lite through commercialization against unit goals of 60 in 2025 and 100 in 2026.
emphasis: unit goals of 60 in 2025 and 100 in 2026

bullets.text: Built ExtrusionStudio, a QC and production system live on all three filament extrusion lines since October 2026, taking it from a LabVIEW proof of concept to a Python service. An offset for the 1-2 minute lag between the laser and the spool ties each reading and alarm to the filament being wound, and print-on-demand thermal labels reducing up to 30% of paper waste per run.

Serve as the technical subject-matter expert across the plant, from industrial electronics on the extrusion lines to low-voltage sensors, and the go-to contact for customer troubleshooting across mechanical faults, electrical faults, and user error.
Assisted in implementation of ProteorPrintOS with SimplyPrint, enabling remote operation and AI-assisted diagnostics with live video and material, waste, and outcome metrics.
Developing an offline version of the ICARUS-Lite and ICARUS-Pro control screen, along with over-the-air automated updates, so customers can run without a Wi-Fi or Ethernet connection.
Co-developed a custom hotend with an outside partner, improving reliability and reducing cost for our materials.

Managed the Coplay location's Microsoft Business Central ERP implementation in five weeks, migrating more than 2,000 items and 150+ products, reconciling inventory counts on the floor, and syncing SKUs with Proteor's global locations.

Led the 2026 inventory count in Business Central, tracing discrepancies to production orders that were processed without verification and never took items out of inventory, then assisted in  implementation of a more warehouse-focused workflow.
Estimate and track the budget of every engineering project, build its BOMs, and maintain each product's unit cost in Business Central.
Present project status, constraints, and budgets at Proteor's monthly USA review with leadership from its global locations.
Act as Hiring Manager for engineering roles, conducting technical interviews and owning final hiring decisions.
Performed risk analysis and mitigations to EU and U.S. standards across ProteorPrint hardware and cloud products.
Re-engineered POSEIDON and ICARUS around one linear-motor motion platform with universal mounts, reaching 4 m/s with 4-micron precision on a 30 kg moving mass.
Managed and expanded the division's IT infrastructure after the Proteor acquisition, standardizing software and internal processes to align with company-wide systems.

context: Acquired by Proteor and is recognized globally as 'Proteor Print'.

bullets.text: Oversaw the product-development pipeline, internal IT infrastructure, and technology strategy while retaining hands-on responsibility for mechanical, electrical, firmware, and software systems, and gave the CEO and the company regular updates as designs and software iterated.
Led the design and launch of the Gen3 POSEIDON, combining a 1 m³ build volume, filament-and-pellet dual extrusion, braked NEMA 34 Z drives, industrial servo XY motion, and a custom gantry.

Designed and hosted a redundant Kubernetes cluster running a self-developed ERP/CRM for orders, inventory, tasks, projects, and customer interactions, with dynamic BOM generation linked to purchasing.
Researched high-speed linear motors that moved a 30 kg payload at 3 m/s with 5-micron accuracy and conducted early 6-axis robotic non-planar printing research.
Improved thermal and acoustic performance through enclosure redesign and component placement, including custom tooling with local fabricators for large-radius aluminum-panel bends.
Integrated a multi-board CAN-bus control architecture that simplified wiring and debugging while supporting larger, modular machines.
Developed independently testable electronics enclosures that could be installed in minutes and coordinated custom harnesses, panel designs, and hardware improvements with vendors.
Designed and released Kratos, a machine engineered to print high-strength above-knee and below-knee prosthetic sockets.
Developed next-generation ICARUS and POSEIDON models with higher-performance components and expanded motion safety through NEMA 34 motors, planetary gearboxes, and power-failure brakes.

Designed THE KRAKEN, a 1 x 2 x 1.5 m hybrid pellet-and-filament gantry printer for a client producing the world's largest 3D-printed statue, and managed CAD, BOM, sourcing, fabrication, assembly, firmware tuning, support, and training.
Diagnosed mechanical and electrical problems during assembly and operation, improving early product reliability.
Tuned, calibrated, and optimized print parameters while documenting design limitations and opportunities for product improvement.
Deliver project-based engineering support for automotive clients and operate a small online store for 3D-printing heat inserts and other printer accessories.
Produced 3D-printed plastic face shields during the COVID-19 pandemic.
Manage the banking and monthly insurance payments for an association of about 80 units.
Help establish a community-focused member board in place of a property management company, remaining Treasurer through a mid-year restructure.
Operated lifts and assisted thousands of guests with ticketing, weather, and slope information.
Performed motor and control safety checks and supported the maintenance team during lift breakdowns.
Built network infrastructure and deployed more than 750 wireless access points across six school buildings.
Accelerated deployment of more than 2,500 Chromebooks by developing an Arduino-based tool to automate setup-data entry.
Coordinated final device distribution with school administrators.
